receptor_A.family: RTK (Tyr protein kinase, EGF receptor/ErbB family)

receptor_B.family: Type I cytokine receptor (IL-6 receptor subunit alpha, CD126)
receptor_B.kinase_domain: NONE — no intrinsic kinase; signals via JAK1/JAK2/TYK2 associated with ICD and through gp130 (IL6ST) co-receptor

co_expression_assessment.verdict: BOTH expressed in aged MF-I and MF-II (the dominant muscle fiber compartments)
co_expression_assessment.note: ERBB4 passes in aged MF-I (pc=0.42, me=0.94) and MF-II (pc=0.43, me=1.06). IL6R passes in aged MF-I (pc=0.24, me=0.41) and MF-II (pc=0.20, me=0.37). Both are expressed in the same aged myofiber compartments, enabling forced-proximity agonism. MuSC expression is low for both (pc<0.10), so the primary target is myofibers, not satellite cells. p_fail raised to 0.10 because IL6R me in aged MF-II is borderline (0.37 < 0.5 threshold).

ecd_asymmetry.note: ECD asymmetry ratio 1.84× (625 vs 339 aa) is substantial but less than H2F (ERBB2 ECD 630 vs FGFR1 ECD 353, ratio 1.78×). The ~286 aa ECD difference positions ERBB4's kinase domain ~429 Å further from the membrane than IL6R's short ICD. This creates a tilted co-clustered interface where ERBB4's kinase domain can reach IL6R's ICD tyrosines, but large adaptors requiring specific docking geometry may be sterically excluded.

receptor_family_check.IL6R: Cytokine receptor (no intrinsic kinase) — requires JAK-associated signaling through gp130/IL6ST
receptor_family_check.verdict: HETEROLOGOUS pair (RTK + cytokine receptor). IL6R itself has no kinase domain, but its signaling partner IL6ST/gp130 (UniProt P40189) has JAK1/JAK2/TYK2 constitutively associated. Under forced proximity, ERBB4's TK domain can transphosphorylate IL6ST ICD tyrosines, while JAK1/2 associated with IL6ST can transphosphorylate ERBB4 C-tail tyrosines. This bidirectional trans-signaling is analogous to the INSR-IL6ST and FGFR1-IL6ST precedents in the experience buffer. NOT a scope limitation — this is a novel but mechanistically defensible pair.

step_2_structural_geometry.geometry_assessment: Both receptors have solved ECD structures. ERBB4 ECD adopts a tethered conformation in the absence of ligand (2AHX). IL6R ECD has the canonical cytokine receptor D1-D2 domain architecture (1N26). The IL6R:IL6:gp130 hexameric complex (5FUC) shows how IL6R brings gp130 into proximity. The ~20 Å GS4 linker is short enough to force close co-clustering of the two ECDs, enabling the ICDs to interact. The 1.84× ECD asymmetry is manageable — similar to H2F's 1.78× ratio.
step_2_structural_geometry.note: Structural evidence exists for both receptors individually, but no co-complex structure exists for this heterologous pair. The geometry inference relies on the H2F and INSR-IL6ST precedents.

transphosphorylation: GRB2 — recruited to phosphorylated SHC1 (ERBB4 substrate) and to IL6ST pY sites created by ERBB4 transphosphorylation; drives RAS-MAPK

SHC1 — canonical ERBB4 adaptor (PMID:16729043, PMID:12716924); phosphorylated by ERBB4 kinase on Y239/Y240/Y317; recruits GRB2-SOS1. Under forced proximity, SHC1 can also be recruited to IL6ST pY sites created by ERBB4 transphosphorylation
GAB1 — scaffolds PI3K and SHP2; recruited to phosphorylated ERBB4 C-tail tyrosines and potentially to IL6ST pY sites; enhanced under bidirectional trans-signaling
PIK3R1 — p85 regulatory subunit of PI3K; recruited to pY sites on ERBB4 (YXXM motifs) and to GAB1; drives PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway
SOS1 — recruited via GRB2 to activate RAS; RAS-GTP drives RAF-MEK-ERK cascade

STAT3 — directly phosphorylated by JAK1/2 associated with IL6ST/gp130; also potentially phosphorylated by ERBB4 kinase (ErbB family can activate STAT3, PMID:20388777). STAT3 is the canonical IL-6 pathway effector; under forced proximity, ERBB4 transphosphorylation of IL6ST ICD may create additional STAT3 docking sites
PTPN11 (SHP2) — recruited to phosphorylated GAB1 and to ERBB4 pY sites; amplifies RAS-MAPK signaling by dephosphorylating RAS pY inhibitors
cis: JAK1 — constitutively associated with IL6ST/gp130 Box1/Box2 motifs; autophosphorylates upon IL6ST clustering; can transphosphorylate ERBB4 C-tail tyrosines
JAK2 — associated with IL6ST; can phosphorylate ERBB4 (analogous to FGFR1-JAK2 interaction, BioGRID:513671)
TYK2 — secondary JAK family member associated with IL6ST
excluded: PLCG1 — requires specific docking geometry at phosphorylated tyrosine sites (e.g., ERBB4 pY sites or IL6ST pY sites). PLCG1's large PH-SH2-SH2-SH3 domain architecture (~130 kDa) requires ~40+ Å spacing for productive docking. The short GS4 linker (~20 Å) combined with the 1.84× ECD asymmetry (625 vs 339 aa) creates a tilted, crowded co-clustered interface where PLCG1 cannot simultaneously access its docking site while the opposing ICD occupies the space. This is directly analogous to PLCG1 exclusion in H2F (ERBB2-FGFR1) and INSR-IL6ST precedents.

biased_pathways: JAK-STAT3 (via JAK1/2 phosphorylation of IL6ST tyrosines → STAT3 recruitment and phosphorylation; enhanced by ERBB4 transphosphorylation of IL6ST ICD)
SHP2-RAS amplification (via PTPN11 dephosphorylation of RAS pY inhibitors)
suppressed_pathways: PLCG1-Ca2+-NFAT (excluded adaptor — steric exclusion due to short linker + ECD asymmetry)

gene_direction_rationale.predicted_up_source: MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT activation drives SRF/MRTF-dependent transcription of muscle structural/contractile genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN, MYL6, TPM2). STAT3 activation upregulates NOTCH3 and TIMP3. PI3K/AKT upregulates IGFBP7. These genes overlap with P2_up (young-enriched) and P1_down (aged-depleted) from the muscle atlas.
gene_direction_rationale.predicted_down_source: MAPK/ERK activation suppresses IEG expression (EGR1, FOS, JUN) via negative feedback (DUSP/MKP phosphatases). STAT3-mediated SOCS3 feedback suppresses inflammatory cytokines (IL32, TXNIP). PI3K/AKT suppresses FOXO-dependent catabolic genes (MYF5, ASB5). These genes overlap with P1_up (aged-enriched) and P2_down (young-depleted). CRITICAL: IEGs (EGR1, FOS, JUN), MYH9, MYF5, IL32, TXNIP are NEVER placed in predicted_up — consistent with past wins and the atlas calibration.
gene_direction_rationale.calibration_check: Pattern matches past wins (ERBB2+FGFR1/2/4): muscle structural genes in predicted_up, aged IEGs in predicted_down. The ERBB4-IL6R pair is predicted to produce a similar transcriptional signature to the winning ERBB2+FGFR pairs because the biased output (MAPK↑, AKT↑, STAT3↑, PLCγ↓) converges on the same downstream TFs (SRF, ELK1, FOXO inhibition, STAT3).

step_confidence_rationale.step_1: Both receptors confirmed expressed in aged myofibers (MF-I, MF-II) from pre-fetched atlas data. ERBB4 is a validated RTK. IL6R is a cytokine receptor requiring gp130/JAK — heterologous but defensible. p_fail=0.10 due to borderline IL6R me in aged MF-II.
step_confidence_rationale.step_2: Both have solved PDB structures (2AHX, 1N26). No co-complex structure for this pair. Geometry inference relies on H2F precedent. p_fail=0.20.
step_confidence_rationale.step_3a: ERBB4 adaptor biology well-characterized (SHC1, GRB2, GAB1, PIK3R1). IL6R/gp130 JAK-STAT pathway well-characterized. Bidirectional transphosphorylation is inferred from analogous RTK-cytokine precedents (INSR-IL6ST, FGFR1-IL6ST). PLCG1 exclusion is geometrically plausible but not experimentally validated for this specific pair. p_fail=0.30.
step_confidence_rationale.step_3b: Reactome API was unavailable during execution. Pathway inference based on known ERBB4 signaling (MAPK, PI3K/AKT) and IL6R signaling (JAK-STAT3). p_fail=0.35.
step_confidence_rationale.step_3c: OmniPath TF-target API was unavailable. Gene direction based on atlas DE lists (P2_up/P1_up) and past win patterns. IEGs correctly placed in predicted_down. p_fail=0.40.
step_confidence_rationale.step_3d: BioGRID ORCS shows ERBB4 and IL6R in cancer cell line screens (drug resistance, fitness) but no muscle-relevant screens. No direct CRISPR support for the predicted gene set in muscle. p_fail=0.45.
step_confidence_rationale.step_4: Gene lists are biologically defensible and calibrated against past wins and atlas DE. The predicted_up/down pattern is consistent with the biased signaling mechanism. However, the heterologous RTK+cytokine pair has no direct experimental precedent, so confidence is moderate. p_fail=0.30.

mechanism_narrative: ERBB4 (RTK, ErbB family) and IL6R (type I cytokine receptor, signals via IL6ST/gp130-JAK) are forced into proximity by a flexible GS4 linker (~20 Å). Under co-clustering, ERBB4's tyrosine kinase domain transphosphorylates IL6ST/gp130's intracellular tyrosines, creating STAT3 docking sites, while JAK1/2 associated with IL6ST transphosphorylate ERBB4's C-tail tyrosines, enhancing SHC1-GRB2-SOS1-RAS-MAPK and GAB1-PIK3R1-AKT signaling. PLCG1 is sterically excluded due to the short linker and 1.84× ECD asymmetry. The biased output (MAPK↑, AKT↑, STAT3↑, PLCγ↓) drives a transcriptional program that upregulates muscle structural genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN) and suppresses aged-muscle IEGs and inflammatory markers (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32, TXNIP), consistent with a rejuvenating shift toward the young muscle phenotype.
